Flight, failure and another try

Crazy Plane
Landing

More power gets you farther. It does not make you land. The interesting choice is when to stop chasing distance and start shaping the approach.

Core steer + boostPayoff wrecks fund upgradesGate the landing strip
The decisionOpening & controlFailure economyCourses & machinesProduct & receptionBuild layer

01 / The landing is the contract

Distance and success pull in different directions.

This is a stunt-flight toy with an upgrade economy. Launch down a ramp, steer an unstable machine, use thrust, collide with a spectacular world, then spend the payout on the next attempt.

The checkered destination turns that spectacle into a skill problem. A farther flight can miss the strip; a shorter, uglier arrival can clear it. Boost therefore has two meanings: it helps cross a gap, and it can carry the craft past the useful contact window. Rotation earns visible stunt rewards, while recovering the approach asks for the same finite height and momentum.

The two tests must stay separate

How far did the attempt travel?

A record can be set beyond the runway. It rewards reach, even when the level stays locked.

Did the craft contact the destination?

A runway contact can finish the level. Breakage and a low final distance do not automatically invalidate it.

This diagram models the observed distinction, not the source's exact collider or distance formula.

The source's collision tolerance is not fully established: touching, crossing and stopping on the strip are not interchangeable implementation rules. For the adaptation, successful chassis contact with a clearly marked goal area will be explicit and testable. The game should never quietly replace that rule with “distance ≥ target.”

02 / The first flight teaches by consequence

The controls arrive before the explanation.

The ramp gives a direction. The yoke gives a promise. The crash shows the cost of not understanding them.

The opening places a cargo aircraft on a descending quarry ramp. PLAY leads into a run; a yoke appears in flight. Between attempts, ENGINE, BOOST and BONUS sit beside the aircraft, each with a level and coin cost. The player is asked to learn flight and an investment strategy almost together.

That is efficient for returning players, but it can make a failed flight ambiguous: was it insufficient power, a bad angle, or a missed target? A large distance number does not answer that question.

Target lesson: show the landing area before the first launch, teach steering during a safe approach, then label the actual cause of the first miss. Keep the retry beside that explanation.
LaunchThe ramp commits the attempt and establishes speed.
Shape the approachSteering and thrust change what the craft can reach.
Read contactParts can break; the chassis continues to travel.
Choose the next tryA payout, an upgrade or a different approach becomes useful.

The target should expose a miss as a spatial fact: under-shot, over-shot or off-line. Sound can reinforce the diagnosis, but the player must understand it with both audio channels muted.

03 / Failure is also production

The wreck buys a better next attempt.

Failure consumes a flight, not all of its value. Distance and stunt performance feed a reward; BONUS turns that reward into faster investment.

The second example is arithmetically clear: (515 + 154) × 6 = 4,014. It does not establish how ×6 was obtained, whether every collection uses the same mechanism, or how advertising was involved. The older interface shows a direct 928 + 93 total instead. Those offers belong to different recorded interfaces and should not be collapsed into one universal payout formula.

ENGINE and BOOST improve the flight side of the loop; BONUS improves the funding side. An income-first strategy can accelerate all subsequent purchases without solving the current landing geometry. That creates a productive tension, but uncontrolled compounding can also drown the skill problem in power and coin inflation.

InvestmentWhy it mattersWhat the adaptation must communicate
ENGINEChanges takeoff capability.More launch speed is useful for a gap, but can make overshooting harder to avoid.
BOOSTChanges the available thrust budget.Show remaining thrust, its activation state and why conserving it can be useful.
BONUSChanges future earning power.Preview the payout change separately from flight capability; do not suggest that it steers the aircraft.

The target keeps earned coins after a miss and makes restart free. It also keeps upgrades across courses as an explicit design choice, with bounded earning growth. Progress should change what the player can attempt rather than repeatedly selling back the same minimum capability.

04 / The course is more than a distance

Geometry and absurd machinery create the variety.

The sequence moves from a quarry through a canyon, an industrial valley, a city, a canal and an icy landscape. Each changes the approach, the objects that can interrupt it, and the comedy of contact.

A readable route can contain a surprising surface.

The canyon puts a railway and bright balloons in the flight space. A plane over a balloon carries a BARREL ROLL 100 banner. The still establishes the encounter and reward text; the exact rebound impulse needs temporal verification.

For the target, a balloon may be designed as an elastic object, but it must be visually different from a destructive bridge. The useful lesson is a consistent surface language, not an unexplained exception.

Breakage is part of the entertainment and part of the feedback. A wing loss should alter the aircraft's subsequent motion in a readable way; floating detached parts alone would deliver the joke without its consequence. Keep the primary chassis identifiable after a collision so the player knows what can still reach the strip.

The target contains the whole six-course circuit, the distinctive vehicle alternatives and a night remix of the circuit. It then supports replay and records. That is a complete adaptation scope, not a claim that the modern source catalogue ends after six courses.

05 / A comic promise, with a costly wrapper

The product sells crashes. The player still needs clarity.

BoomBit dates the title to 19 July 2021 and presents it as hypercasual spectacle rather than realistic piloting. The demanded player is willing to experiment with steering, repeat short failures and invest in capability; the visual fantasy makes those failures entertaining. Official game page.

Build the complete mobile web adaptation of Crazy Plane Landing described in this HTML's Build layer: an absurd flight toy where the player launches a breakable machine, steers and budgets boost toward a marked landing strip, earns from spectacular misses, then invests in the next attempt. Preserve the distinction between a distance record and a valid landing, and reproduce the choice illustrated by EP-01. Deliver the entire six-course circuit, all target vehicle alternatives, connected upgrades, night remix, replay, persistence and polished feedback as one portable offline HTML.

Use a portrait browser window and touch controls from the adaptation bridge; keep the craft, landing area and miss cause readable with the thumb and HUD present. Design the first 20 minutes from #roblox-hooks, keeping player agency over the approach. Follow the art/audio plan, EN/RU switch, independent music/SFX sliders and bug.games platform plan. Design and tune the stated open space without removing complete-game content. Parse all sections, extract and inspect the required embedded figures, then plan, build, play-test and fix the whole product in this task. A first-course demo is not completion.

Reading procedure: parse the complete HTML structurally, including collapsed content, without loading base64 into text context. Extract embedded images to the builder's working folder, open them with an image tool, verify every required figure ID and compare literal states with the rule that cites them. The donor and source images are references, not game assets. An inability to view images or hear production audio must be reported; packaging alone does not prove understanding or game fidelity.

Load-bearing core statements

  1. K1: The player sees a reachable landing zone, chooses steering and thrust, and changes the approach; excessive reach may turn a promising flight into an overshoot.
  2. K2: A distance record and a valid destination contact are independent. A broken craft can still clear when its main chassis reaches the valid zone; off-zone distance alone never clears.
  3. K3: A failed flight produces useful earnings. Spending on capability or income changes the next attempt without automatically solving the landing decision.
  4. K4: Stunt rewards compete with approach stability, and visible collision damage changes subsequent travel. The intact silhouette, breakage and surviving chassis tell the player what happened.

EP-01 · farther is not closer to success

S-B canyon example: the captured wreck at 469s reads 566M and NEW HIGHSCORE, while its marker stays separate from NEXT LEVEL (failure state). S-A industrial example: 603M record at 325s is followed by a separate later 461M successful state at 420s (record, clear). These are different attempts/contexts, not one continuous causal clip. Their common supported lesson is the separation of record and valid landing. Target episode: fly beyond the canyon strip without contact, receive a record and payout but no clear; retry with a shaped approach, contact the marked goal with the main chassis and gain Continue, even if parts break and final distance is lower.

Design space and principles

GapPreserveBuilder freedomCheck
Flight and steering mathThrust/steering shape a recoverable approach; overshoot remains possible; craft profiles matter.Choose arcade lift/drag/rotation, camera lead, thrust consumption and meaningful profile differences. Use fixed steps and bounded collision work; no mandated engine.Adjacent inputs produce different readable approaches; compare low/high capability and two craft through ordinary touch play.
Goal eligibility and damageSpatial landing success is separate from reach; the primary body remains meaningful after breakage.Author goal colliders/tolerances and joint thresholds. Detached wings never clear on behalf of the main chassis in the target. Define contact once; permit rough valid arrivals.EP-01, off-zone debris, edge contact, fast crossing and a slow slide each resolve once.
Economy and accessEarn → spend → changed next attempt; income upgrade differs from capability upgrades.Choose bounded curves, craft unlock milestones and fair course scaling. Source 128000/256000 are reference prices, not mandatory target grind.Every course and vehicle reached without payment; Bonus investment cannot eliminate steering; repeated failures cannot deadlock progress.
Course content and recurrenceSix distinct geometries, absurd craft, a meaningful night variation and replay.Author full routes, obstacles, approach alternatives, night readability and mastery goals. No need to invent all unseen current source levels.Ordinary circuit completion plus replay; night changes visibility while retaining clear goal signals.
Feedback, sound and end conditionsPreparation → flight → contact → readable consequence → recovery.Design actual sound/music and timing; define settlement/out-of-bounds watchdog without arbitrary infinite wait. Pause interrupts control safely.Listen and play on target phones; silence remains intelligible; a map escape returns a result and free retry.

Principles (interpretations): create situations by changing the approach geometry; teach a cause before adding another obstacle; reward spectacle even when the goal is missed; escalate capability and precision together; keep a visible reason to correct the next attempt. Repeated attempts should differ because of the player's choice, not an invisible forced-failure rule. The builder records major design decisions and revisions in its own notes and validates them through play; no extra authoring approval stage is needed.

Short-session loop and touch map · Designed

Entry at the current course → first tap launches → continuous drag steering and optional boost → stunt/contact feedback → result and stable payout → Retry or Continue. Tune an early active flight to roughly 15–30 seconds and a failure-to-next-launch path to two simple taps or fewer. These are target pacing goals, not durations measured from edited videos. Upgrade access, records, craft ownership and course progression carry over; individual flight velocity, damage, thrust consumption and stunt chain reset.

Touch / contextInspect, select, commit, cancelReach / protection
Portrait entryTap Launch commits once; drag within the steering surface changes pitch/roll after launch.Primary craft/goal above the lower thumb zone; source orientation is translated. Play at 390×844 and in a smaller iframe; no fullscreen dependency.
BoostTap on its distinct button toggles active thrust; second tap cancels. Optional press-and-hold from a second thumb stops on release.Minimum target starting size 56 CSS px; pressed/remaining-budget readout. One-handed path remains practical; disambiguate taps from steering drags.
Upgrade / craftTap shows benefit, current versus next and cost; explicit Buy spends once. Selecting owned craft is free. Back cancels.No purchase/selection triggered by a drag. A disabled purchase states required and owned coins; not only a color.
Outside / extra pointersTouch outside a control does nothing. Ignore extra pointers unless the supported boost hold owns one.Pointer capture continues steering when the thumb leaves its starting area. pointercancel releases all active control.
Pause, focus, rotationPause freezes simulation and mutes continuing cues. Hidden tab, platform sheet or orientation change pauses once; returning shows Resume.Neutralize steering/thrust, never run a catch-up flight. Manual pause is not dismissed by platform resume; resize preserves the saved course and result state.

Set touch-action only on the play control surface; ordinary settings and menus scroll. Keep responsiveness and legibility over literal yoke artwork. Designed test targets: first controllable frame within 3 seconds after local load on the declared test device; no visible delayed steering beyond 100ms in measured input-to-render sampling; sustained 30fps or better on the declared baseline phone. Measure actual file size, peak memory, startup, responsiveness and frame rate, then report device/browser and any misses. These are production targets requiring measurement, not authoring-run results.

Settings are target-game requirements

A small Settings entry offers English / Russian and separate touch-usable Music and Sound effects volume sliders. Translate all player-facing onboarding, HUD labels, results, reasons, errors, purchases/availability, pause and credits. Switching during play preserves the current flight and updates visible text immediately. Save language and both levels as device preferences; never combine them with monotonic progression merges.

Each channel has its own gain and actual zero silence; adjusting one does not change the other. Platform mute multiplies both to zero without overwriting their saved values. Start/resume audio only after a gesture; a suspended context does not block play. Settings must not become a first-run modal. This English report does not require a document translation switch; EN/RU is a requirement of the future game.

CheckpointPlayer action and visible feedbackReason to continue

Art, signal and audio direction · Designed

Use a bright miniature aviation playground: clean stylized geometry, expressive hybrid craft and strong terrain silhouettes. Keep the launch–approach–breakage grammar; replace cluttered promotional UI with a restrained flight HUD. Portrait chase framing always shows the main chassis, upcoming obstacle and landing cue; lead the camera toward the destination before descent. The lower thumb band must not cover the chassis contact shadow, goal outline or warning. Comedy belongs in the vehicle and collision consequence, while the choice stays legible.

Accepted archive visual transfer: Flip Trickster's bounded landing outline remains visible beside a failed contact. Its source figures #fig-contact and #fig-failure were extracted and viewed; donor HTML Teardowns/Неотправленные/Hypercasual Teardown — Flip Trickster — EN.html. Same mechanism: spatial travel must intersect a visible region. Translate to a checkered rim and simple depth/contact shadow; do not copy the donor's assets, target rings, score multipliers, character or input. Risk and before/after check: ask where contact was required after a miss, then verify the next correction and collider/outline agreement through play. This is a Designed candidate, not an implemented or retention-proven solution.

Element / functionEvidence anchorTarget asset/source kindCoherence and phone check
Aircraft / surviving bodyhybrid, freighter, wreckOriginal or licensed stylized models/drawn projections. Code geometry is valid if it serves expressive silhouettes. Separate attached parts and identifiable chassis.One scale/material family; consistent warm lighting; silhouette readable during roll and after wing loss. No NASA/BoomBit marks or ripped models.

Balloon softness, solid bridge, water and goal have distinct form.Reduced background contrast, no high-frequency textures behind labels. Night variant preserves the same danger/contact grammar.

Preparation lean, controlled thrust plume, contact dust/sparks, debris and clear confirmation.Anticipation → contact → consequence → recovery. Confetti never implies success outside goal; debris never masks chassis or duplicates goal/reward.
SFX / event identityOriginal source timbre unavailableLicensed recordings, generated or procedural original cues chosen for flight toy; separately verify file rights.Normalize perceived loudness, vary repeated impacts, limit overlapping debris cues. Listen on phone speaker; separate music/SFX gain.
Music / playful momentumNo independently heard music referenceOriginal commissioned/generated or licensed light instrumental loop. Target brief: buoyant percussion and short melodic phrases, low density during approach.One musical family; seamless looping, restrained result accent, reduced intensity in pause. No asserted source BPM or identical sound match.

Event sheet: full audio production, without a fidelity claim

TriggerDesigned cue / visual partnerPriority / recoveryAsset status
Launch / ramp accelerationShort mechanical release + rising engine tone; craft lean and wake establish commitment.Steering-ready state visible; engine level follows speed, not a canned whole-flight sample.Not supplied. Source engine descriptions are report-only.
Boost start / stop / emptyDistinct thrust burst and sustained bed, plume with remaining budget; stop fades promptly; empty has a brief dry cue.Essential state signal; never mask target warning; pause stops looping sources.Original/licensed production required.
Stunt completedSmall rising tick; label and one increment. Ground tumbles do not stack identical chimes.Below contact/result in mix; cap overlapping notification density.Original/licensed production required.
Impact / part breakMaterial crunch + short snap; part detaches, main chassis stays readable.Impact takes priority; brief restrained camera response, no prolonged control lock. Distinct soft balloon contact.Original/licensed production required.
Miss / clear / payoutNeutral miss tag; bright two-stage clear accent; soft count-up, then stable total.Diagnosis and Retry/Continue available before ornament finishes; avoid shaming stingers or loud repeated failures.Original/licensed production required.
Pause / resume / menuQuiet UI tick and lower music intensity; resume a suspended context only after a gesture.No hidden sound after mute, pause or tab loss; clean one-time restart.Original/licensed production required.

Asset sourcing: shortlist actual direct asset pages with author, file-specific licence, format and fit. Prefer CC0/public domain, MIT/Apache and OFL; record attribution-required material and put required notices inside the final game. Download actual assets, not previews; maintain ASSETS.md internally and verify the running phone presentation and sound. Skip non-commercial, no-derivatives, unclear or ripped assets. A teardown frame is an analytical reference, never a production texture. No art or audio assets have been produced in this authoring run.

bug.games plan · native measurement, complete free base

Runtime reference checked directly with bug.games sdk_docs on 6 October 2026. The future game remains one inline-asset HTML; game.json is platform metadata beside it when hosted, not another gameplay implementation. No hosted game, products or publication were created.

Omit cover/screenshots until original game artwork exists; do not publish teardown evidence as promotional art. minutes: 3 is a proposed session label to calibrate with real use, not measured average playtime. The eight moments above are ≤12 and appear in play order. Report each once on the stable transition with progress.moment(name); persist local reached state and reconcile safely.

Runtime boundary: boot the free core immediately. Before importing, detect standalone/offline mode; import /sdk/bloomplay.js conditionally only in the actual platform integration. Check isEmbedded, use init({timeout, preload:["save","settings"]}) and distinguish no platform from an initialization error. No third-party analytics or API fetches. If play starts during the handshake, remember the actual state and re-emit its start after connection. Call loaded() when interactive from ordinary code, and gameplayStart() only on a real flight; gameplayStop() on pause/result/hidden state. Menus are not gameplay. Idempotent pause handlers prevent duplicate stops.

Outside bug.games, never request an SDK path from file:// or an arbitrary iframe; use a bounded local diagnostic event log and local guarded saves. A plain embedded preview must not hang waiting for an absent platform. On platform use the SDK save layer or safe versioned reconciliation: failed reads are not empty accounts; settings use their own key. Never erase confirmed progress after a transient read failure. OnPause reasons include hidden/signin/purchase/dialog/page; an active manual pause survives onResume. Apply platform mute without losing device music/SFX preferences.

Custom eventExact one-time triggerNecessary propertiesQuestion
approach_resultStable flight result resolved once, before count-up.course_id, variant, craft_id, attempt_index, result (clear/under/over/off-line/bounds), distance_m, stunt_count, boost_fraction_usedAre misses caused by reach, lateral error or unreadable recovery?
retry_choicePlayer presses Retry from a settled failed result.course_id, attempt_index, last_result, upgraded_since_resultDoes a readable failure lead to a purposeful next attempt? Counts alone are not retention.
upgrade_committedA confirmed soft-coin debit completes once.stat, old_level, new_level, cost, course_idWhich investment changes the next result? Compare matched attempts without assuming causality from correlation.
craft_changedOwned craft selection becomes active at the ramp.from_id, to_id, course_idDo players use alternatives rather than only the strongest-looking silhouette?
lesson_appliedThe first instructed steering correction / boost stop / valid goal contact occurs.lesson_id, course_id, attempt_indexCan the first loop teach its load-bearing decisions?
settings_changedA confirmed language/channel preference changes, debounced at gesture completion.setting, language or volume_bucketAre translations/audio controls discoverable? Avoid raw drag floods and personal data.
extra_previewOnly if a future built cosmetic preview is opened.extra_id, availability_stateIs cosmetic interest present? This is not a sale or revenue.

Do not duplicate automatic bp_page_view or native gameplay events as custom launches. Per-attempt IDs prevent repeated results on animation or reconnect; moments have their own once-reached rule. QA uses ordinary play and the local diagnostic log, then the real platform preview before publication.

Optional Extras · none in the complete base specification

No Extras screen or active product is required. A possible future hangar-livery durable cosmetic would add coordinated paint schemes beyond the full free craft roster. It is planned, unbuilt, unavailable; omit it from products. Do not show a price, Buy button, teaser after failure or a promise of future sale. If built later, let the player discover it voluntarily in craft selection and preview/revert it without changing flight stats or outcomes.

Future sale states: confirmed ownership wins over catalogue visibility; sellable only when returned by monetization.getProducts(), using its returned price. A successful catalogue that omits an item means unavailable, with no claim why. Offline means purchases unavailable; service errors mean temporarily unavailable. Failed entitlement checks never revoke last confirmed ownership. A preview grants no durable item. SDK purchase(id) owns the transaction; grant exactly once only after confirmed success and verified entitlement, then restore input/audio. Cancellation, error and insufficient balance grant nothing. Only built and tested extras enter platform review. No ad API, coin top-up or creator payout model was verified, so none is assumed.

Acceptance cases frozen before implementation

Source-backed expectations and Designed target behavior are distinguished here. Test the actual portable HTML through real inputs, then the hosted platform preview. No build tests have run in this authoring task.

Case / setup and inputExpected stable resultBasis and evidence
C1 · Fresh portrait entry; tap Launch, drag, start/stop boostFirst action works without sign-in, purchase or title maze. Steering and thrust alter the approach; one-hand control is viable. No accidental double launch or scroll stealing.Designed controls/pacing preserving K1, R1. Test 390×844 and a small iframe, muted as well as audible.
C2 · EP-01; fly beyond the runway without main-chassis contactRecord and payout can occur; course does not clear. Result says over-shot when that geometry is true; Retry stays free.Checked result distinction R2, 566M; spatial diagnosis Designed.
C3 · Crash early; collect; retry twiceReward credited once, stable breakdown, bank retained, same course restarts. Buying income differs from buying thrust; no payment required.First payout R3; target credit timing, free retry and retention Designed.
C4 · Reach goal with broken main chassis; test wing-only contact, edge contact and a fast passEligible main body clears once; detached wing alone never clears. Outline agrees with collider; rough contact does not require an intact plane. Bounds escape resolves to a result.432M broken clear checked; eligibility tolerances and timeout Designed. Goal.
C5 · Complete all six courses and the full night remix through normal playEvery route, obstacle family, approach alternative and Continue transition exists; no debug unlocks substitute for balance. After completion, replay/records remain useful.Complete target scope Designed from shown course grammar; source entire catalogue/endless limit unknown.
C6 · Earn and use all nine craft alternativesAll accessible without purchase; contrasting profiles remain viable. Selection changes the craft once, not a paid unlock on accidental tap.Target catalogue/access Designed; verified and report-only source identities listed in inventory.
C7 · Inspect/Buy/Cancel upgrade, exact balance and insufficient balanceInspection/cancel spend nothing; a Buy deducts once and increases one stat. Disabled state explains missing coins. Other stats/preferences unaffected; progress persists.R4 escalating next-price labels checked; target settled debit and persistence Designed.
C8 · pointercancel, focus loss, manual pause, rotation and platform pause/resumeSteering/thrust neutralize; simulation does not jump forward; main chassis/result preserved. Resume requires an intentional gesture; no double result, reward or gameplay edge.Designed lifecycle. Source continuous timing unverified.
C9 · Switch EN↔RU in flight/result; set music 0 / SFX 70, then music 60 / SFX 0; reloadAll current player text translated immediately, flight intact, each zero channel actually silent and sliders independent. Language and both levels restore. Platform mute does not overwrite values.Designed Settings requirement; inspect long Russian strings and listen to each channel independently.
C10 · First 20 minutes on a phone, with no debug money or forced successCheck H1/H2 milestones; player sees goal, cause and correction. Repeated attempts demonstrate different approaches; no automatic landing or forced purchase.Designed hypotheses, not retained-player evidence. Verify the accepted Flip Trickster outline in ordinary motion, thumb/HUD present.
C11 · Reload after upgrade, unlock, course clear and resultBank/ownership/access/records restored without replaying payouts; partial flight returns safely to ramp. Blocked local storage gives usable play and an honest local-save warning. Platform failed read never overwrites known account save.Designed persistence; source save not demonstrated.
C12 · SDK absent/error/delayed connect; event and moment receiptComplete offline file boots without failed network requests. Native gameplay edges/moments and custom events appear at declared triggers once. Delayed init receives current state; no automatic event duplicated.SDK plan checked; actual platform preview must be tested before publication.
C13 · Future cosmetic only if built: empty catalogue, sellable, owned, failed checks and offline; mock purchase outcomesNo Buy outside a returned sellable product. Ownership preserved on service error; cancel/error/insufficient coins grant nothing; confirmed success once and reload restore. Preview reverts and leaves flight unchanged. Current base has no empty shop.Designed conditional extra integration; a mock does not establish real sales or approval.

Delivery checks for the built game: double-click the final one-file HTML on desktop; no CDN/sibling fetch, all fonts/images/audio decode, representative circuit play and save work. Reliable phone testing uses the same file served over HTTPS on an actual device; do not promise file-viewer execution on phones. Record performance and sound tests separately from semantic fidelity. Fullscreen, orientation lock and vibration are optional enhancements. Debug late-state checks supplement but never replace ordinary completion.

Source limits that remain material: exact pitch/roll/yaw and manual/automatic boost behavior; stable purchase debits/refusals, vehicle-specific upgrade persistence and reset boundaries; precise valid-contact collider and detached-part behavior; complete present-day level/vehicle catalogue; full rebound, air-traffic, train and cargo-breakage dynamics; source sound/music and unedited durations. The downloaded-media route did not yield a usable clip. These limit faithful reconstruction claims, while the explicit design-space contract keeps the complete target build actionable.

The local-library pilot used two problems and queries: launch boost overshoot landing target retry and upgrade income failure reward explain feedback. Flip Trickster's goal outline was accepted after pixel inspection. Hoop World was rejected as overlapping the source's existing contact/continuation signals; Slap Kings' loss payout was rejected as redundant and its continuous retry boundary unverified; Slots & Daggers was rejected because a slot/turn investment cycle does not resolve an airborne approach. No donor images are production assets, and no retention result is asserted.

Packaging and authoring QA establish that the single document renders and its evidence is accessible. No separate receiving model was run in this task, so receiving-side understanding is not experimentally certified. No game was implemented, so actual game fidelity, balance, first-20-minute success, sound quality and real platform analytics remain future acceptance work.
